newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-INDIA ON BRINK OF DEFEAT VS S.AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA ON BRINK OF DEFEAT VS S.AFRICA.

text.p: India lost Sachin Tendulkar and Mohammad Azharuddin within five balls of each other but still limped through to lunch on the fifth and final day of the second test in Cape Town on Monday.
The pair were dismissed in the fourth and fifth overs of the morning to leave India in dire straits at 61 for five as they set out on their task of batting out the day to save the match.
By lunch they had moved to 110 for six , 317 runs short of their theoretical target to level the three test series following their 328-run defeat in Durban.
Much had depended on Tendulkar and Azharuddin -- first innings centurions and the most accomplished batsmen of the Indian line-up -- as India resumed at 52 for three.

Tendulkar got his side off to the worst possible start, however, when he attempted to hook a Brian McMillan bouncer from wide outside the off stump, succeeding only in giving a top edged catch to Lance Klusener at mid-on to be out for nine.
Four balls later Azharuddin aimed a loose drive at a ball from Allan Donald and Andrew Hudson gobbled up the catch at third slip to leave the Indian innings in tatters.
Saurav Ganguly resisted for the best part of two hours before pushing at a delivery from Shaun Pollock to give McMillan a straight forward catch at second slip.
V.V.S. Laxman (21 not out) who was struck three times on the helmet and Anil Kumble (11 not out) clawed their way to the interval with an unbeaten eighth-wicket partnership of 23.
